neighbours.label: Gospel narrative about Herod, Pilate and Jesus (New Testament Passion and nativity accounts)
fire: When Herod heard that a king had been born in Bethlehem, he was deeply troubled.
Pilate asked Jesus whether he was the king of the Jews, and Jesus answered him.
Herod the Tetrarch had John the Baptist arrested and later beheaded.
The chief priests handed Jesus over to Pilate, who questioned him before the crowd.
Joseph took Mary and the child and fled to Egypt to escape Herod.
Then Pilate washed his hands before the crowd and released Barabbas to them.
Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus and sent him back to Pilate in a robe.
The wise men were warned in a dream not to return to Herod.
quiet: When Caesar heard that the legions had crossed the Rhine, he was deeply troubled.
The senator asked Cicero whether he would defend the consul, and Cicero answered him.
Nero had the philosopher Seneca arrested and later forced him to take his life.
The generals handed the prisoner over to Augustus, who questioned him before the crowd.
Aeneas took his father and his son and fled from burning Troy.
Then the emperor raised his hand before the crowd and spared the gladiator.
Caligula and his guards mocked the envoy and sent him back to Judea empty-handed.
The Greek sailors were warned by an oracle not to return to Athens.

notes: Card: all top examples are New Testament passages with Herod, Pilate and Jesus; peaks on function words inside them.
